title: Introducing new and effective catalysts for the synthesis of pyridazino[1,2-a]indazole, indazolo[2,1-b]phthalazine and pyrazolo[1,2-b]phthalazine derivatives
author: Amirmahani, Mahmoodi, et al.

steps.title: Screen reaction parameters (Table 1)
steps.instruction: Test a series of catalyst types, loadings, temperatures and times under solvent‑free conditions to identify the optimal conditions for the four‑component condensation of aldehyde, hydrazine hydrate, succinic/phthalic anhydride and 1,3‑dicarbonyl compound.

substeps.instruction: Entry 1: No catalyst, solvent‑free, 100 °C, 24 h → 0 % yield.
Entry 2: [TEAH][OAc] 0.05 mmol, solvent‑free, rt, 24 h → 10 % yield.

steps.title: Perform optimal four‑component condensation
steps.instruction: Carry out the model reaction using the optimal conditions identified (20 mol % [TEAH][OAc], solvent‑free, 80 °C, 20 min) to obtain the desired heterocyclic triones or carboxylates.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 1.0 mmol of the aldehyde (e.g., benzaldehyde).
Add 1.1 mmol of succinic anhydride (or phthalic anhydride, depending on target scaffold).
Add 1.0 mmol of the 1,3‑dicarbonyl compound (e.g., dimedone, ethyl 3‑oxobutanoate, etc.).
Add 0.20 mmol (20 mol %) of the ionic liquid catalyst [(CH₂CH₂OH)₃NH][CH₃COO] ([TEAH][OAc]).
Mix the solid reagents thoroughly in a dry reaction vessel (no solvent).
Seal the vessel and heat it to 80 °C (oil bath or heating block).
Maintain the temperature for 20 min while stirring; monitor progress by TLC if desired.
After 20 min, remove the vessel from heat and allow it to cool to room temperature.
Add an appropriate organic solvent (e.g., ethyl acetate) to the reaction mixture to dissolve the product.
Filter the mixture to separate the ionic liquid (which can be recovered and reused).
Wash the filtrate with water, then dry over anhydrous Na₂SO₄.
Evaporate the solvent under reduced pressure to afford the crude product.
Purify the product by recrystallization from a suitable solvent or by column chromatography.
Characterize the isolated compound by melting point (M.P.), IR, and ¹H NMR, comparing with literature data.

steps.title: Apply protocol to diverse substrates (Table 2)
steps.instruction: Repeat the optimal reaction using various aldehydes (R¹) and 1,3‑dicarbonyl partners (R²) as listed in Table 2 to obtain the corresponding heterocyclic products.

substeps.instruction: For each entry, use 1.0 mmol of the chosen aldehyde (R¹) and 1.0 mmol of the chosen 1,3‑dicarbonyl compound (R²) together with 1.0 mmol hydrazine hydrate and 1.1 mmol anhydride, keeping the catalyst amount (0.20 mmol [TEAH][OAc]) and conditions (solvent‑free, 80 °C, 20 min) identical.
Follow the work‑up and purification steps described above.
Record the isolated yield (percentage) for each product as shown in Table 2 (e.g., 6a 90 %, 6b 92 %, …, 7k 87 %).
